doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bird, Ben Webster and the 1950s decline
title: Young Chicago altoists in Bird's mode who died young
summary: They try to recall a Bird-like altoist, with talk of Nicky Hill and drug casualties of the period.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: These cats who were here in this area, like – they’re younger people, like Nicky Hill and . . .
. . . and – what was the name of the alto player my father used to tell me about? Kind of Bird-like. I don’t know if he got shot stealing a t.v. or something, or was
that Nicky Hill? What was the name of that cat? He died young, alto player, in a Bird kind of mode.
Let’s see. Did he give you any kind of description about height or the skin color?
No, no. I think he said that he got shot stealing a t.v. out of a church, but I don’t know if he was talking about Nicky Hill or that guy.
They had one cat that was really on Bird. He was one of the main ones playing up there one night when I was playing with Bird.
Uh – George is much better on names than I am, but this cat . . .
I’ll think of his name in a second.
I know him very, very well. I’m certain that’s the . . .
Everybody was – that was another dying period, redlining there. A lot of musicians got fouled up with dope and whatnot, and they went right out of here.
